maya (docs): quick heads-up — mkdocs linkcheck failing on the latest deploy. CI shows a bunch of broken fragment links where anchors were percent-encoded (soft-hyphen / unicode punctuation).
kevin (eng): hmm, can you paste one example from the logs?
maya (docs): here — from linkcheck output: `URL https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/serving#multi‑tenant` reported 404 because the built html has `#multi%E2%80%91tenant` (soft-hyphen encoded).
kevin (eng): ugh, that makes sense after the migration. The slugifier/anchor generator changed for some headings.
maya (docs): quick probe: I ran `grep -R "%E2%80%91" site/ | head` and found ~12 files.
kevin (eng): short-term fix suggestion: normalize those encoded chars during the build step. e.g.:
```bash
# naive fix during deploy (awk/sed)
find site -name "*.html" -exec sed -i 's/%E2%80%91/-/g' {} +
```
kevin (eng): longer-term: add a small mkdocs plugin to post-process generated ids or configure the markdown slugifier to match the old behavior.
maya (docs): agreed. also adding a tiny test to our docs CI to fail if linkcheck finds percent-encoded hyphens in fragments.
olga (devex): I can open the PR for the sed quick-fix + CI assertion, pinging @kevin for review. :+1:
maya (docs): thanks @olga — please target `docs/deploy-fixes`. Include the grep and a one-liner in the PR description so reviewers can reproduce.
ci-bot: linkcheck job re-run queued on branch docs/deploy-fixes (job #214).
kevin (eng): once PR is up I can sketch the mkdocs plugin and a follow-up issue to remove the sed hack. :eyes:
maya (docs): sounds good. tagging this thread for the release checklist so we don't miss the redirect backfill. :shipit:
olga (devex): PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482 — includes sed fix + CI assertion + short test doc. assigning @kevin for review.
kevin (eng): reviewing now, will push a small tweak to use perl -0777 -pe instead of sed so multi-line ids are handled.
maya (docs): awesome, thanks both. once merged I'll trigger the publish and double-check the live site anchors.
